_metadata.purpose: Admission decisions for `dom` rules (UNI-224 Phase A evidence gate). Rules listed here are NOT evaluated by the engine. Everything not listed is admitted.
_metadata.why_a_denylist: Phase A measured 1,600 dom rules against 4,214 real institutions. 1,585 landed in UNVALIDATED/PLAUSIBLE and auto-admit; only 13 needed adjudication. A denylist of the failures is far smaller and more legible than an allowlist of the survivors.
_metadata.adjudication_note: Corroboration against a tech's non-dom evidence is ONE-WAY: high corroboration proves genuine, low corroboration proves nothing (Google Font API corroborates at 2% because `link[href*='fonts.g']` is delivered by <link>, not script — the dom rule is the better detector). Rejections below are therefore based on DIRECT inspection of what the selector actually matched in the corpus, not on low corroboration.

denied.reason: Catastrophically over-broad. Zero of the top matched class tokens are Element UI. Actual matches: mega-nav__level-three-plus-link (551), field--label-hidden (536), ubermenu-item-level-2 (120), level-3, carousel-item — i.e. any class containing the substring 'el-', which 'level-', 'label-', 'carousel-' all do. Element UI is a Vue component library; these are Drupal/WordPress menu classes.

Over-broad: 'default' contains 'fa'. Genuine FA tokens do match (fas, fa-solid, fa-brands, svg-inline--fa), but so do elementor-section-height-default (470), elementor-size-default (424), aem-GridColumn--default--12 (213), ubermenu-item-layout-default (188). Fires on ~48% of institutions. Narrowing to [class*='fa-'] would likely be sound — but that is a pattern edit, not an admission decision, so the rule is denied as written.

denied.name: type
denied.reason: Matches any application/* link type. Of the matched values only application/rss+xml (113) and application/atom+xml (1) are RSS; application/json (68), application/json+oembed (65), application/rsd+xml (58) and application/wlwmanifest+xml are not. Roughly 63% of matches are wrong.

admitted_after_review.why: RE-ADJUDICATED 2026-08-09 (UNI-226). Previously DENIED as "form[name='formLogin'][action='login.aspx' i][id='formLogin']\;confidence:40" — but the only defect was the trailing '\;confidence:40', UPSTREAM WAPPALYZER MODIFIER SYNTAX the importer never stripped, which made querySelectorAll reject the selector. UNI-226 now strips modifiers at load, so the selector reads form[name='formLogin'][action='login.aspx' i][id='formLogin'] and parses. On its merits it is ADMITTED: three attribute constraints on a single form element is about as specific as a dom rule gets, and it was never denied for breadth. ⚠️ Note the denylist is keyed on the selector STRING — once stripping landed, the old entry stopped matching and the rule would have gone live silently. Recording the decision here instead of leaving it to a key mismatch.
meta[property*='og:'] is definitively Open Graph. ~66% of university homepages carrying OG tags is correct, not implausible.
link[href*='fonts.g'] matches fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com — definitive. Corroborates at only 2% because the tech's other evidence is script-based; the dom rule is the better detector.
[fetchpriority] is a real HTML attribute; the detection is accurate even if 'Priority Hints' is a marginal thing to call a technology.
script[class*='yoast-schema-graph'] is a specific, dedicated Yoast marker. 0% corroboration reflects its other patterns not firing, not a false positive.
link[rel='manifest'] is definitive for a web app manifest.
div.swiper-wrapper is Swiper's own class name.
